block.title: A CPUID source that never ends its leaf 4 list makes glibc's startup read out of bounds
block.p: The Hello proof now starts at __libc_start_main, and the second thing that function does is call init_cpu_features. That function asks the processor about itself with CPUID, so a proof that it never panics has to cover every answer the processor could give. One sequence of answers makes the Fil-C build of user glibc 2.44 panic.

The function get_common_cache_info in sysdeps/x86/dl-cacheinfo.h counts the threads that share a cache. On an Intel processor it reads CPUID leaf 4 one subleaf at a time. Since glibc 2.44 it first looks in a small table of answers that handle_intel saved earlier. Lines 851 to 864 are the start of the loop:

The loop ends at line 901 with while (check). It stops early when an answer reports cache type 0, and check becomes zero once the awaited cache levels have been reported. Nothing else bounds i, and the table leaf4 has 16 rows.

A processor describes one cache in each answer and marks the end of the list with an answer whose cache type is 0. The loop relies on that end mark, and a processor that answered as follows would never give it.

ul.li: The vendor is GenuineIntel, the highest basic leaf is at least 4, and bit 28 of leaf 1 EDX is set.
Leaf 2 answers EAX = 1 and zero in the other three registers. With that answer handle_intel finds no cache and saves no leaf 4 answer.
Leaf 4 answers EAX = 0x21 for every subleaf, which describes a level 1 data cache.

block.p: The loop is then waiting for a level 2 cache that never comes. After 2^31 queries the counter wraps to the least int. The test on line 857 compares that negative number with a saved count of zero and succeeds, and line 858 reads cache->leaf4[i] about 32 GiB below the table.

The C source is not what runs, so I also looked for the failing instruction in the compiled function. The compiled function keeps the counter in a 32-bit temporary. One block adds one to it and lets the sum wrap. Another block compares it with the saved count as a signed number. A third block scales it to an offset in the table and checks that four bytes are readable at that address.

That last check fails when the counter is negative. A failed bounds check is a Fil-C panic, so the process stops there and reads nothing. Anyone who wants to read the code can find it in HiAtexitTypedGE.v. The function is named glibc_libc_start#get_common_cache_info there, and the check binds chk9 in its block L90.

claim.p: Nobody has seen this panic on a machine, because it needs a CPUID source that no real processor provides. I found the path with a program that follows the compiled code and keeps a range for each value. I wrote that program for this proof and have not yet proved it correct, so I confirmed the path by reading the compiled code and the C source.

block.p: No real processor answers this way. Intel's manual says that leaf 4 returns zeros for a subleaf past the last cache, and zeros have cache type 0. The answers have to come from a hostile or broken CPUID source, such as a hypervisor that intercepts the instruction.

Upstream glibc has the same loop. The table of saved answers arrived in glibc 2.44, and the lines above are the same in the glibc-2.44 tag and in upstream's current master branch. Fil-C's copy of the file differs from the tag only where two bsr assembly statements became __builtin_clz. Through glibc 2.43 the loop called __cpuid_count (4, i++, ...) with no table, so an endless list could only keep it running. In a native build the overflow of i is undefined behavior, and I have not tested what such a build does.

A fix would bound the counter, for example by leaving the loop when i reaches the number of rows. That is a change to user glibc, which this repository treats as a toolchain change that needs its own review, and it is not this proof's to make.

Because the fix is not ours to make, the proof of init_cpu_features has to assume that the processor ends its list. This is a design that is not written yet. The assumption says that a leaf 4 query with subleaf 0x7fffffff reports cache type 0, which is the weakest fact that stops the counter before it wraps. It will be a boolean ow_leaf4_ends of the OS world, and the contract in OsCpuid.v will give the fact to a caller when the boolean is true.
The same unproved program reports no other failing check in init_cpu_features or in the functions it calls, whatever CPUID and XGETBV answer.
